gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-cascadia-: Cascadia Mono stands its letters like pins in a wide board, with curves as stout as its stems. And Eight Bit Dragon strides above it, a towering lowercase with a faint swell in every round letter.

gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-lexend-ex: Eight Bit Dragon strides along with a towering lowercase and a slight swell in each bowl. Lexend Exa has no hairline against its stems, while the heading earns its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-lexend-me: Towering lowercase is what Eight Bit Dragon does best, swelling moderately in its rounds. But Lexend Mega, a sans-serif, does its best with round bowls that never swell or thin.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-lexend-pe: Eight Bit Dragon strides across wide-set letters, its towering lowercase carrying a middling swell in each stroke. And Lexend Peta, with wide-mouthed c shapes and no thinning in its curves, keeps whole paragraphs moving.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-lexend-te: Lexend Tera draws every letter with one plotter-pen width and sets them apart like stepping stones. Beneath Eight Bit Dragon, body text feels open and unhurried, line after line.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-lexend-ze: Eight Bit Dragon strides in with a towering lowercase and mid-level stroke contrast, bold and adventurous. Lexend Zetta counters with ribbon-cut strokes of constant width, tracked wide and tall-bodied.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-montserra: Towering lowercase, relaxed stride: Eight Bit Dragon barely thins its strokes between stems and joins. But Montserrat Alternates makes every diagonal as stout as every upright, with a c bent open like a paperclip.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-cascadia-m: Gaps break each word into single letters in Electroharmonix, whose curves stay open-handed and low in contrast. And Cascadia Mono runs rope-like in every stem, bowl and tail, its compact capitals blending into lowercase.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads wide and sturdy, its x-height generous. Over a whole page, its rope-fine strokes keep going without a hairline, a quiet backdrop to the gapped, commanding letters of Electroharmonix.
